subject: mathematics
question_text: If θ is not an integral multiple of π/2, prove that tan θ + 2 tan 2θ + 4 tan 4θ + 8 cot 8θ = cot θ.

mark_split.label: Prove cot θ − tan θ = 2 cot 2θ
Apply it at θ, 2θ and 4θ and add

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 47(i), book p.96. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1 + 1 gives one mark to the lemma cot θ − tan θ = 2 cot 2θ, which is the engine of the whole chain, and one to applying it three times and adding. SOURCE CONDITION TOO WEAK — RECORDED, NOT SILENTLY REPAIRED: the book's stem says θ is not an integral multiple of π/2, but that does not keep every ratio in the identity defined. At θ = π/4, tan 2θ = tan(π/2) is undefined; at θ = π/8, cot 8θ = cot π is undefined; neither π/4 nor π/8 is an integral multiple of π/2. The true requirement is sin 8θ ≠ 0, that is θ ≠ nπ/8, because sin 8θ = 8 sinθ cosθ cos2θ cos4θ, so that one inequality is exactly what keeps tan θ, tan 2θ, tan 4θ, cot 8θ and cot θ all defined at once. The card prints the stem as the book has it and states the sharper condition in the answer's own lines, where the student reads it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A prints ten very short answers of 2 marks each and the student writes all ten, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations supplies two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Prove cot θ − tan θ = 2 cot 2θ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Prove the lemma from the definitions, then rearrange it as tan θ = cot θ − 2 cot 2θ, which is the form the chain needs.
steps.memory_tip: cot minus tan is twice the cot of the double angle. Rearranged as tan θ = cot θ − 2 cot 2θ, it turns every tangent into two cotangents.

recall.must_convey: That cot θ − tan θ = 2 cot 2θ is proved from the definitions and rearranged as tan θ = cot θ − 2 cot 2θ.
accept: cot theta minus tan theta is two cot two theta
write both as cos over sin and sin over cos and combine
the top becomes cos two theta and the bottom is half sin two theta
cot minus tan ante two cot two theta, adi lemma
rearrange it as tan theta equals cot theta minus two cot two theta

steps.why: One small identity is enough for the whole question. cot θ − tan θ = 2 cot 2θ, written as tan θ = cot θ − 2 cot 2θ, replaces each tangent in the chain by a difference of two cotangents, and differences arranged like that cancel when added.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that sin θ cos θ is half of sin 2θ.

steps.label: Apply it at θ, 2θ and 4θ and add
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the lemma three times, at θ, 2θ and 4θ, each already multiplied by the coefficient the question uses. Then add.
steps.memory_tip: Write the lemma three times, at θ, 2θ and 4θ, each times its coefficient. Only the first and the last cotangent are left.

recall.must_convey: That the lemma is written at θ, 2θ and 4θ with the given coefficients, the inner cotangents cancel on adding, and 8 cot 8θ is moved across.

multiply each one by its coefficient two and four
the middle cotangents cancel leaving cot theta minus eight cot eight theta

steps.why: Each line is the same lemma at a doubled angle, already multiplied by the coefficient the question prints. Written that way every inner cotangent appears once with a plus and once with a minus, so only the first and the last are left.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply the lemma by 2 and by 4.
Cancelling cot θ as well, although it appears only once.
